name: Database and Data Management
description: Designing, building and running the systems organisations keep their data in. ⚠⚠⚠ The finding that shapes every decision here: Florida has essentially NO undergraduate database degree. The dedicated code produces 62 credentials a year and 61 of them are ONE master's programme at UWF — so the route into this work runs through computer science, information technology or information systems, and the database specialism is assembled from courses rather than handed over as a major.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠⚠ THE DEGREE DOES NOT EXIST, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Data Modeling/Warehousing and Database Administration (11.0802) is recorded at 5 Florida public institutions and produces 62 credentials a year — University of West Florida 61 at MASTER'S level, Hillsborough 1 associate, and Daytona State, Miami Dade and Florida Polytechnic recording programmes that awarded nothing in the year measured. ⚠ So an eighteen-year-old cannot enrol in a Florida public bachelor's in database administration, because there is not one to enrol in. ⚠⚠ What exists instead is the course layer, and it is large: 21 Florida public institutions teach the upper-division database course, plus 9 carrying COP2700 at introductory level and a substantial Oracle and SQL Server certificate tier in the state colleges. ⚠⚠⚠ AND IT IS TAUGHT IN THREE DIFFERENT COLLEGES UNDER THREE DIFFERENT PREFIXES, under SEVEN statewide numbers — COP3703, COP4703, COP3710, COP4710 (computer science), ISM3212, ISM4212 (information systems, in the business school) and CTS4408 (applied computer technology). ⚠ SEVEN institutions carry more than one of the seven, and FIU and USF each carry THREE — which is the proof that these are not one course filed differently but genuinely different courses for different audiences. ⚠⚠ So the practical advice is: pick the degree for the rest of what it teaches, then make sure the database course you take is the one your target employer's work resembles. The theory course, the business course and the administration course are not substitutes.

cips.note: Data Modeling/Warehousing and Database Administration — 5 Florida public institutions and 62 credentials: UWF 61 at master's level, Hillsborough Community College 1 associate. ⚠⚠ Daytona State, Miami Dade and Florida Polytechnic record programmes under this code that awarded nothing in the year measured — Florida Polytechnic's is a bachelor's. ⚠ Claimed so those five institutions are visible, but the honest reading is that the state has one live programme and it is a graduate one.

related.note: ⚠⚠ The main route, and the one that leads to the better-paid half of the work. Database ARCHITECT — the design side — posts a $139,500 median against database administration's $104,620, and the design courses (COP4710, COP3710) sit in the computer science college. ⚠ 16 Florida institutions award computer science against one live database programme.

⚠ The widest route by far — 39 Florida institutions — and the one the Oracle and SQL Server certificate tier attaches to. ⚠⚠ It is the fastest way into a database job and the slowest way to the architect half: BLS projects database ADMINISTRATORS at 0% growth over 2025-35 and architects at +9%. Enter here, but aim past it.

⚠⚠ The third route, and the one students overlook. ISM3212 and ISM4212 are the same subject taught from the business side — data as something an organisation decides with, rather than a system to be optimised. ⚠ Ten Florida institutions carry those two numbers, and for analytics and reporting work it is the better preparation.

⚠ The adjacent destination, and the boundary is real: a data scientist builds models from data, a database architect builds the thing the data lives in. ⚠⚠ They share the SQL and the warehousing courses — CAP4770 Data Mining is carried by 9 Florida institutions and CAP4774 Data Warehousing by 3 — and diverge on statistics.

⚠ Named for a specific course: CIS4368 Database Security and Audits runs at FAMU, FGCU, USF and UWF, and database security is where the two fields actually meet. ⚠⚠ A database professional who can speak to auditors is paid differently from one who cannot.
